Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean: 1. City is the City of Pangkalpinang.

2. City Government is the mayor as the element of Regional Government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.

3. Mayor is the Mayor of Pangkalpinang

4. Regional People's Representative Council, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional People's Representative Council of the City of Pangkalpinang.

5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order.

6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills abilities so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective abilities.

7. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.

8. All Forms of Discrimination against Women are all forms of Discrimination that include the territorial dimension (disaster areas, conflict areas, border areas, underdeveloped areas, remote areas, and others), age dimension (productive age, elderly, and others), and special dimensions (persons with disabilities, workers, and others).

9. Violence against Women is any action that violates, inhibits, eliminates the enjoyment and neglects women's human rights.

10. Domestic Violence is any act against a woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household.

11. Elimination of Violence against Women is a guarantee provided by the Regional Government to prevent violence, prosecute perpetrators of violence and protect victims.

12. Elimination of Domestic Violence is a guarantee provided by the state to prevent domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence.

13. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

14. Companion is a parent or representative of an institution that has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

15. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.

16. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

17. Gender Justice is a process of being fair to men and women.

Article 30

(1) Forms of violence against women include: a. physical violence;

b. sexual violence;

c. economic violence; and

d. psychological violence.

(2) The form of physical violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disabilities to a person's body, unconsciousness and or causes death.

(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or undesirable manner, forcing relations with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

(4) The form of economic violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is the neglect of women in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.

(5) The form of psychological violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

(6) Every woman victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 32

(1) Forms of protection against violence toward women include:

a. medical protection;
b. legal protection;
c. medico-legal protection (forensic medicine); d. economic protection; and
e. psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of the victim carried out by medical and paramedical personnel.
(3) The form of legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medico-legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is in the form of services for skills and to provide economic access so that victims of violence can be independent.
(6) The form of psychological protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter e is in the form of psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems through assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims.

Article 29

(1) The City Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against women in the form of: a. collecting data and information about victims of violence and laws and regulations; b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women;

c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection for victims of violence;

d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for victims of violence; and

e. preparing reports on the implementation of protection for women victims of violence.

(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence against women, the City Government is obliged to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:

a. establishing and facilitating the implementation of integrated service institutions for victims by involving community elements; and
b. encouraging public awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The City Government in carrying out obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

Article 28

(1) Every woman victim of violence has the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, the City Government and the community.

(2) In the event of violence, every victim has the right to obtain health services and assistance, both psychologically and legally as well as obtain guarantees for their rights related to their status as women.

CHAPTER VII

PROTECTION OF WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE Part One

General

Article 31

Every victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

Article 24

(1) The implementation of protection for domestic women workers in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel treatment, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity and exploitation in employment relationships.

(2) Domestic women workers as referred to in paragraph (1) obtain protection for: a. recognition of rights, wages and decent working conditions; b. health and employment social security; c. access to information and legal consultation services; and d. opportunity to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

Article 39

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into effect, Regional Regulation of Pangkalpinang City Number 6 of 2014 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence (Regional Gazette of Pangkalpinang City Year 2014 Number 6) as amended by Regional Regulation of Pangkalpinang City Number 6 of 2018 concerning Amendment to Regional Regulation of Pangkalpinang City Number 6 of 2014 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence (Regional Gazette of Pangkalpinang City Year 2018 Number 6), is revoked and declared invalid.

Article 14

(1) The implementation of women in the field of health as referred to in Article 8 letter f health services in order to undergo a reproductive life and sexual life that is healthy, safe and free from coercion and/or violence.

(2) Health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. health services during the period before pregnancy, during pregnancy, during childbirth and after childbirth; b. pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health; and
c. reproductive health services.
(3) Health services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches.

CHAPTER VI

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 22

(1) The implementation of protection for women with disabilities in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel treatment, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity and freedom from exploitation.

(2) Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) obtain the right to protection for:

a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal assistance, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 6

(1) The City Government is obliged and responsible for the implementation of women's empowerment and protection.

(2) Efforts for women's empowerment and protection as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. determination of policies, programs, and activities; b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.

(3) Efforts for women's empowerment and protection as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out in an integrated manner.

Part Three

Forms of Violence and Protection

Article 19

(1) Women have the right to obtain special protection from things that threaten their safety and/or health.

(2) Special protection is given to women because their reproductive function is guaranteed and protected by law.

(3) The City Regional Government facilitates health protection in accordance with regional financial capacity.

(4) The form of health protection for women as referred to in paragraph (3) is further regulated in a Mayoral Regulation.

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean: 1. City is the City of Pangkalpinang.

6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills abilities so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective abilities.

7. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.

8. All Forms of Discrimination against Women are all forms of Discrimination that include the territorial dimension (disaster areas, conflict areas, border areas, underdeveloped areas, remote areas, and others), age dimension (productive age, elderly, and others), and special dimensions (persons with disabilities, workers, and others).

9. Violence against Women is any action that violates, inhibits, eliminates the enjoyment and neglects women's human rights.

10. Domestic Violence is any act against a woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household.

11. Elimination of Violence against Women is a guarantee provided by the Regional Government to prevent violence, prosecute perpetrators of violence and protect victims.

12. Elimination of Domestic Violence is a guarantee provided by the state to prevent domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence.

13. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

14. Companion is a parent or representative of an institution that has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

16. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

17. Gender Justice is a process of being fair to men and women.

Article 24

(1) The implementation of protection for domestic women workers in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel treatment, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity and exploitation in employment relationships.

(2) Domestic women workers as referred to in paragraph (1) obtain protection for: a. recognition of rights, wages and decent working conditions; b. health and employment social security; c. access to information and legal consultation services; and d. opportunity to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

Article 32

(1) Forms of protection against violence toward women include:

a. medical protection;
b. legal protection;
c. medico-legal protection (forensic medicine); d. economic protection; and
e. psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of the victim carried out by medical and paramedical personnel.
(3) The form of legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medico-legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is in the form of services for skills and to provide economic access so that victims of violence can be independent.
(6) The form of psychological protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter e is in the form of psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems through assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims.

Article 22

(1) The implementation of protection for women with disabilities in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel treatment, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity and freedom from exploitation.

(2) Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) obtain the right to protection for:

a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal assistance, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 28

(1) Every woman victim of violence has the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, the City Government and the community.

(2) In the event of violence, every victim has the right to obtain health services and assistance, both psychologically and legally as well as obtain guarantees for their rights related to their status as women.

Article 29

(1) The City Government is obliged and responsible to carry out efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against women in the form of: a. collecting data and information about victims of violence and laws and regulations; b. conducting education on anti-violence values against women;

c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection for victims of violence;

d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for victims of violence; and

e. preparing reports on the implementation of protection for women victims of violence.

(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence against women, the City Government is obliged to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:

a. establishing and facilitating the implementation of integrated service institutions for victims by involving community elements; and
b. encouraging public awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
(3) The City Government in carrying out obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

Article 32

(1) Forms of protection against violence toward women include:

a. medical protection;
b. legal protection;
c. medico-legal protection (forensic medicine); d. economic protection; and
e. psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of the victim carried out by medical and paramedical personnel.
(3) The form of legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medico-legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is in the form of services for skills and to provide economic access so that victims of violence can be independent.
(6) The form of psychological protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter e is in the form of psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems through assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims.

Article 30

(1) Forms of violence against women include: a. physical violence;

b. sexual violence;

c. economic violence; and

d. psychological violence.

(2) The form of physical violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disabilities to a person's body, unconsciousness and or causes death.

(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or undesirable manner, forcing relations with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

(4) The form of economic violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is the neglect of women in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.

(5) The form of psychological violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

(6) Every woman victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 1

Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.

8. All Forms of Discrimination against Women are all forms of Discrimination that include the territorial dimension (disaster areas, conflict areas, border areas, underdeveloped areas, remote areas, and others), age dimension (productive age, elderly, and others), and special dimensions (persons with disabilities, workers, and others).

9. Violence against Women is any action that violates, inhibits, eliminates the enjoyment and neglects women's human rights.

10. Domestic Violence is any act against a woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household.

11. Elimination of Violence against Women is a guarantee provided by the Regional Government to prevent violence, prosecute perpetrators of violence and protect victims.

12. Elimination of Domestic Violence is a guarantee provided by the state to prevent domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence.

13. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

b. sexual violence;

c. economic violence; and

(1) Forms of violence against women include: a. physical violence;

a. rehabilitation and social reintegration; and

Article 30

(1) Forms of violence against women include: a. physical violence;

b. sexual violence;

c. economic violence; and

d. psychological violence.

(2) The form of physical violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disabilities to a person's body, unconsciousness and or causes death.

(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or undesirable manner, forcing relations with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

(4) The form of economic violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is the neglect of women in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.

(5) The form of psychological violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

(6) Every woman victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 24

(1) The implementation of protection for domestic women workers in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel treatment, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity and exploitation in employment relationships.

(2) Domestic women workers as referred to in paragraph (1) obtain protection for: a. recognition of rights, wages and decent working conditions; b. health and employment social security; c. access to information and legal consultation services; and d. opportunity to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

Article 32

(1) Forms of protection against violence toward women include:

a. medical protection;
b. legal protection;
c. medico-legal protection (forensic medicine); d. economic protection; and
e. psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of the victim carried out by medical and paramedical personnel.
(3) The form of legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medico-legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is in the form of services for skills and to provide economic access so that victims of violence can be independent.
(6) The form of psychological protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter e is in the form of psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems through assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims.

6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills abilities so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective abilities.

7. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.

8. All Forms of Discrimination against Women are all forms of Discrimination that include the territorial dimension (disaster areas, conflict areas, border areas, underdeveloped areas, remote areas, and others), age dimension (productive age, elderly, and others), and special dimensions (persons with disabilities, workers, and others).

9. Violence against Women is any action that violates, inhibits, eliminates the enjoyment and neglects women's human rights.

10. Domestic Violence is any act against a woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household.

11. Elimination of Violence against Women is a guarantee provided by the Regional Government to prevent violence, prosecute perpetrators of violence and protect victims.

12. Elimination of Domestic Violence is a guarantee provided by the state to prevent domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence.

13. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

14. Companion is a parent or representative of an institution that has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

15. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.

16. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

17. Gender Justice is a process of being fair to men and women.

(1) Forms of violence against women include: a. physical violence;

b. sexual violence;

c. economic violence; and

(4) The form of economic violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is the neglect of women in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.

(5) The form of psychological violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

(2) In the event of violence, every victim has the right to obtain health services and assistance, both psychologically and legally as well as obtain guarantees for their rights related to their status as women.

Article 32

(1) Forms of protection against violence toward women include:

a. medical protection;
b. legal protection;
c. medico-legal protection (forensic medicine); d. economic protection; and
e. psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of the victim carried out by medical and paramedical personnel.
(3) The form of legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medico-legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is in the form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.
(5) The form of economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is in the form of services for skills and to provide economic access so that victims of violence can be independent.
(6) The form of psychological protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter e is in the form of psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems through assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims.

Part Seven

Article 30

(1) Forms of violence against women include: a. physical violence;

b. sexual violence;

c. economic violence; and

d. psychological violence.

(2) The form of physical violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disabilities to a person's body, unconsciousness and or causes death.

(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or undesirable manner, forcing relations with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

(4) The form of economic violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is the neglect of women in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.

(5) The form of psychological violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

(6) Every woman victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 22

(1) The implementation of protection for women with disabilities in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel treatment, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity and freedom from exploitation.

(2) Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) obtain the right to protection for:

a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
c. accessibility of information, legal assistance, mobility, social services; and
d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 25

(1) The implementation of protection for women as family economic providers in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, negative stigma and economic empowerment for women as family economic providers.

(2) Women as family economic providers as referred to in paragraph (1) obtain the right to protection for:

a. discriminatory actions and efforts to weaken the function of women as family economic providers;
b. strengthening capacity and recognition as family economic providers in their environment; and c. accessibility to economic and financial institutions.

Article 24

(1) The implementation of protection for domestic women workers in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel treatment, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity and exploitation in employment relationships.

(2) Domestic women workers as referred to in paragraph (1) obtain protection for: a. recognition of rights, wages and decent working conditions; b. health and employment social security; c. access to information and legal consultation services; and d. opportunity to obtain knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean: 1. City is the City of Pangkalpinang.

5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order.

6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills abilities so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective abilities.

7. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.

8. All Forms of Discrimination against Women are all forms of Discrimination that include the territorial dimension (disaster areas, conflict areas, border areas, underdeveloped areas, remote areas, and others), age dimension (productive age, elderly, and others), and special dimensions (persons with disabilities, workers, and others).

9. Violence against Women is any action that violates, inhibits, eliminates the enjoyment and neglects women's human rights.

10. Domestic Violence is any act against a woman that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household.

11. Elimination of Violence against Women is a guarantee provided by the Regional Government to prevent violence, prosecute perpetrators of violence and protect victims.

12. Elimination of Domestic Violence is a guarantee provided by the state to prevent domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence.

13. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.

14. Companion is a parent or representative of an institution that has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

15. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.

16. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

17. Gender Justice is a process of being fair to men and women.
